_comment: The county record score (scripts/county_record_score.py): how restrictive a county is for wind, solar and battery storage, read from its own published record rather than from its resemblance to other counties. Hand-edited; no process writes it. Added 2026-10-21 after the October 16 case studies scored Linn County, IA (two contested solar projects approved, rules in force no stricter than severity 2) above Nicholas County, KY and Cherokee County, KS (each with a moratorium in force). The resemblance score (config/county_model_registration.json) is kept, unchanged, as the profile prior for counties with no record. Like that score, this one is internal: nothing on a page or in a county report reads it without a separate decision by Price.

instruments._note: Points for one restriction instrument (rows sharing an instrument_id are one instrument; its severity is the highest of its rows). Points = severity points x currency x jurisdiction x technology breadth.
instruments._currency_note: unknown is the share of status-unknown instruments found in force by the 2026-10-21 status sample (60 NREL instruments, seeded and stratified by technology and severity, two readers each): 40 of the 47 settled were in force, 89 percent weighted by group size; counting the 4 whose record matched no adopted instrument as not in force gives about 78 percent. 0.85 lies between the two.

jurisdiction._note: A county-wide instrument governs the whole county; a city, town, township or village instrument governs part of it.

instruments._others_note: A county's instrument points are its largest instrument's points plus others_weight times the sum of the rest, so a second and third instrument add to the score without a long list of minor rules outweighing one moratorium.

projects._note: Contested projects placed in the county, by outcome. A confirmed outcome counts fully, a recorded but unconfirmed one half. Approvals lower the score: a county that has approved contested projects is shown to be open under its rules.
projects._approval_note: Approvals can take off at most this share of the county's instrument and zoning points, and never take the score below the points of a severity 4 county-wide instrument in force: a moratorium in force outweighs earlier approvals.

zoning_transition._note: In these states counties may stay unzoned, the county is the body that zones unincorporated land, and no statute gives an unzoned county a siting permit or siting power over wind or solar outside zoning (general home-rule or ordinance powers, which Kansas counties also hold, do not count) (config/county_zoning_authority.json, zoning_transition; a state siting body may still review large plants). A county that moves from no zoning to zoning while projects are proposed is setting up the means to restrict them, so the move counts as a county-wide instrument at the severity below, in force from the date drafting began until counts_for_years_after_adoption after the code is adopted. tests/test_county_record_score.py keeps this list equal to the states marked in county_zoning_authority.json.

A consultant (Confluence) is drafting its first zoning code for the county planning commission, under a draft comprehensive plan that lists wind farms, solar farms, battery storage and data centers as high-impact uses and records that many residents supported prohibiting them or regulating them strictly.

counties.summary: Crawford County zoned only a southeast part of the county from 1967; the rest of its unincorporated land had no zoning. After moratoriums on wind, solar, battery storage and other uses, the commission voted on July 10, 2026 to zone all unincorporated land and to ban future wind projects (Motions 26-319 and 26-320). On September 25, 2026 it sent the regulations back to the Planning and Zoning Board (motion 26-453), and no resolution has adopted them. Counted here as a transition because most of the county is moving from no zoning to zoning.

build_out._note: Plants built without a recorded fight are uncontested approvals: the record holds only the projects that drew opposition, so without these a county that approved everything quietly looks the same as one never asked. Counted from EIA-860M (one source, so no plant twice): solar, wind or battery storage plants of at least min_mw, operating or under construction, whose year (online, or planned online) is since_year or later and no earlier than the year of the county's latest instrument in force, so a plant that predates a rule is not read as that rule's approval. A county's contested projects that advanced are assumed to be among its plants, so only plants beyond that number count. Each counts as the 'built' outcome in projects.points, inside the same approval caps.

no_county_zoning._note: States whose counties have no general zoning power, so no county can adopt a siting rule for unincorporated land; only its cities can, inside their limits. In these states an empty record is evidence in itself: the county government cannot restrict, so a county with no record is weighed at evidence_weight.no_county_zoning against its profile prior instead of being scored on the prior alone. Each state names its evidence: the verified state_policies.csv row, or the statute and the two readings recorded in config/county_zoning_authority.json. except_counties lists the counties of those states that zone anyway (by local act) or must permit wind or solar under a local act; they are scored as in any other state.

evidence_weight._note: How far the record speaks for itself. combined = weight x record points + (1 - weight) x profile points, where profile points are the mean record points of all counties in the same decile of the resemblance score, a county with no record counting as zero (a floor, since most counties have never been examined). A county with no record and no negative check is scored on its profile alone.

tiers.name: closed
tiers.label: Closed: a moratorium or ban in force, or rules that act as one, county-wide

tiers.name: severe
tiers.label: Severe: rules likely to block most projects

tiers.name: restrictive
tiers.label: Restrictive: material rules, or blocked projects

tiers.name: regulated
tiers.label: Regulated but open: rules in force, projects approved under them

reference_counties._note: The counties of the October 16 case studies, printed in the report so a change to the rubric shows its effect on them. The October 2026 review of the four reports read Nicholas and Cherokee as much less friendly than Linn.
